title: IdeaScientist: Orchestrating Agents for Grounded Scientific Ideation
abstract: Despite rapid progress in automating scientific research, generating promising and well grounded research solutions remains a central challenge. We isolate research ideation as a standalone task and build our solution on the intuition that a challenge in one field can often be addressed by a mechanism that solved an analogous challenge in another. Accordingly, we introduce IdeaScientist, which decomposes ideation into gap finding, innovation, and report writing, and trains each role with reinforcement learning. These roles identify limitations in related work, draw solution intuitions from analogous problem settings, and develop those intuitions into complete research proposals. To facilitate discovery of insights across domains, we construct the Svalbard Idea Vault, a corpus of 2.77M decomposed research ideas for retrieval, training, and temporally controlled evaluation. Our evaluation restricts access to literature available before a cutoff date and assesses how closely proposed directions align with those later explored in 15K papers authored by human researchers. On Qwen3.6-27B, IdeaScientist outperforms the strongest open-source autoresearch baseline by 14.0%, driven mainly by gains in novelty. On this 27B open backbone, IdeaScientist even outperforms Claude Code SDK with Claude-4.8-Opus and Codex SDK with GPT-5.4, by up to 5.9%.

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: In a hypothetical graduate seminar on Autonomous Scientific Research, today’s lecture is on IdeaScientist: Orchestrating Agents for Grounded Scientific Ideation. Recent systems such as The A-I Scientist and Towards Execution-Grounded Automated A-I Research connect idea generation to code, experiments, and papers. IdeaScientist takes a different angle: it treats proposing an idea as a capability worth evaluating on its own. The team includes researchers from Carnegie Mellon University and Meta Reality Labs. Yes, Noah?
segments.zh: 在一场假设的关于自主科学研究的研讨课上，今天的讲座主题是IdeaScientist：编排智能体实现有据可依的科学创意生成。最近的系统，比如The A-I Scientist和Towards Execution-Grounded Automated A-I Research，把创意生成和代码、实验以及论文联系了起来。IdeaScientist则换了个角度：它把提出一个想法本身当作一种值得单独评估的能力。这个团队里有来自卡内基梅隆大学和Meta Reality Labs的研究人员。好，Noah？

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Hi Professor, why separate ideation from actually running experiments?
segments.zh: 教授您好，为什么要把构思想法和实际跑实验分开呢？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Because successful execution does not necessarily mean the initial idea was strong. A system might produce useful results from an incremental proposal, or fail to implement a promising one. By evaluating proposals before implementation, the authors aim to distinguish idea quality from engineering and execution. Their benchmark asks whether a system can generate grounded directions resembling methods that researchers later pursued, while recognizing that resemblance is not the same as scientific value.
segments.zh: 因为执行成功并不一定意味着最初的想法就很强。一个系统可能从一个渐进式的提案中产出有用的结果，也可能没能实现一个有前景的提案。通过在实施之前评估提案，作者希望把想法的质量和工程与执行区分开来。他们的基准测试问的是，一个系统能否生成有依据的研究方向，使其类似于研究人员后来实际采用的方法，同时也承认相似并不等同于科学价值。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The paper defines ideation as producing a proposal from a problem and an unresolved challenge. That challenge might be about the quality of a model’s output, or about the research process, such as latency or privacy. A good proposal should connect to prior work, explain its mechanism, and describe how it could be tested. The central tension is familiar: stay too close to existing work and proposals may be incremental; stray too far and they may lack grounding.
segments.zh: 这篇论文把构思定义为：针对一个问题和一个尚未解决的挑战，提出一个方案。这个挑战可能关乎模型输出的质量，也可能关乎研究过程本身，比如延迟或隐私。一个好的方案应该与已有工作建立联系，解释其机制，并说明如何对它进行检验。核心矛盾很熟悉：离已有工作太近，方案可能只是渐进式的；离得太远，又可能缺乏根基。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: So the key is to borrow a useful mechanism without just copying another field?
segments.zh: 所以关键在于借用有用的机制，而不是直接照搬另一个领域？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Exactly. IdeaScientist makes cross-domain analogy an explicit part of its process. First, it finds a specific gap in literature close to the target problem. Then it searches other areas for a mechanism that addresses a structurally similar challenge. The analogy must be made concrete: what mechanism is being borrowed, what structure is shared, how will it be adapted, and what assumptions or risks does the adaptation introduce?
segments.zh: 没错。IdeaScientist把跨领域类比明确变成了流程的一部分。它先在与目标问题相近的文献里找到一个具体的空白，然后去其他领域寻找能解决结构相似挑战的机制。这个类比必须落到实处：借的是什么机制，共享的是什么结构，打算怎么改造，改造又会引入哪些假设或风险？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The system coordinates three proposal-producing agents. A gap finder identifies limitations in closely related papers and supports each gap with evidence. An innovator searches for mechanisms that might transfer from other settings. A report writer turns the resulting idea into a structured proposal, including related-work comparisons, method details, an evaluation plan, falsifiable predictions, and limitations. Separating these roles makes the process easier to inspect and lets the authors train each role independently.
segments.zh: 这个系统协调三个负责提出方案的智能体。一个找缺口，在密切相关的论文里识别局限，并为每个缺口提供证据支撑。一个做创新，寻找可能从其他场景迁移过来的机制。一个写报告，把由此产生的想法整理成结构化的提案，包括相关工作对比、方法细节、评估方案、可证伪的预测以及局限性。把这些角色分开，能让整个过程更容易被检查，也让作者可以独立训练每个角色。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Two supporting agents help manage evidence and critique. A paper reader digests full-text papers in an isolated context, so the other agents do not need to process entire papers repeatedly. A reviewer returns evidence-based objections to candidate ideas. The orchestrator can revisit earlier stages in response. This resembles a research group’s workflow: focused specialists contribute separate analyses, while a coordinator decides which objections warrant another round of investigation.
segments.zh: 两个辅助智能体负责管理证据和提出批评。一个论文阅读器在隔离的上下文中消化全文论文，这样其他智能体就不需要反复处理整篇论文。一个审稿人对候选想法返回基于证据的反对意见。编排器可以据此重新回到之前的阶段。这类似于研究小组的工作流程：专注的专家各自贡献独立的分析，而协调者决定哪些反对意见值得再轮调查。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: Quick question: what data teaches the agents to make these proposals?
segments.zh: 快速问一句：是什么数据教会这些智能体提出这些方案的？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The authors build the Svalbard Idea Vault from roughly 4.7 million papers, about 2.8 million of them with full text. They decompose papers into problem, challenge, gap, intuition, and proposal, creating 2.77 million structured ideas. For training and testing, they use 14,977 methodological machine-learning papers published from January 1, 2026 onward. Their proposal versions hide reported results, retaining research directions and methods rather than experimental outcomes.
segments.zh: 作者从大约470万篇论文中构建了Svalbard Idea Vault，其中约280万篇有全文。他们把论文拆解为问题、挑战、空白、直觉和提案，创建了277万个结构化想法。在训练和测试中，他们使用了2026年1月1日以后发表的14977篇方法论机器学习论文。他们的提案版本隐藏了已报告的结果，保留的是研究方向和方法，而不是实验结果。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: Training also matters because proposal quality has no simple automatic answer key. The authors train the gap finder, innovator, and report writer separately with reinforcement learning and rubric-based rewards. A judge assesses qualities such as specificity and feasibility; other signals compare generated artifacts with paper-derived references and check citation overlap. Protocol checks penalize violations. At test time, systems can retrieve only pre-cutoff literature, while the held-out target papers remain hidden and internet access is disabled.
segments.zh: 训练之所以重要，还因为提案质量并没有一个简单的自动答案标准。作者用强化学习和基于评分标准的奖励，分别训练缺口发现器、创新器和报告撰写器。一个评判器负责评估具体性、可行性等质量维度；其他信号则把生成的产物与论文衍生的参考进行比对，并检查引用重叠情况。协议检查会对违规行为进行惩罚。在测试阶段，系统只能检索截止日期之前的文献，而留出的目标论文保持隐藏，互联网访问也被禁用。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: On the paper’s primary judge, IdeaScientist-Trained scores 74.6 overall, compared with 73.5 for its base version and 60.6 for the strongest listed open-source baseline, Deep Scientist, on the same backbone. The trained system’s average novelty score is 68.8, and its proposal-quality score is 80.4. Its same-domain novelty measure reaches 70.9. The pattern suggests training especially helps novelty, rather than simply improving every aspect of proposal writing equally.
segments.zh: 在论文的主要评审模型上，IdeaScientist-Trained 总体得分为74.6，而同一骨干网络下，其基础版本为73.5，所列最强开源基线 Deep Scientist 为60.6。训练后系统的平均新颖性得分为68.8，提案质量得分为80.4。其同领域新颖性指标达到70.9。这一模式表明，训练尤其有助于提升新颖性，而不是简单地在提案写作的各个方面都带来同等改善。

segments.speaker: Noah
segments.en: How convincing is the evaluation if its reference proposals come from papers published later?
segments.zh: 如果参照的提案来自后来发表的论文，这样的评估有多大说服力？

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: It provides a useful retrospective test, not a complete definition of good science. Matching later human research shows that a system can recover directions people pursued after the literature cutoff; it does not prove those directions are feasible, impactful, or correct. The authors also use blind human comparisons on 50 problems. IdeaScientist-Trained is preferred over most systems, but not significantly over Deep Scientist, and annotator agreement is moderate, with a correlation of 0.56.
segments.zh: 它提供了一个有用的回溯性测试，但并不是对什么是好科学的完整定义。与后来的人类研究相匹配，说明一个系统能够重新找到文献截止之后人们所追求的方向；但这并不能证明这些方向是可行的、有影响力的或正确的。作者还对50个问题做了盲测人工比较。IdeaScientist-Trained比大多数系统更受青睐，但相比Deep Scientist并没有显著优势，而且标注者之间的一致性只是中等，相关系数为0.56。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: This design adds a distinct question to the wider automated-research conversation. The A-I Scientist emphasizes a connected pipeline from ideas through experiments and writing, while IdeaScientist isolates proposal generation so its stages can be examined before execution. Its analogy-based approach also connects to theories of creative cognition: useful novelty can come from recognizing a shared structure across domains. The practical contribution is a testable workflow for finding gaps, searching for mechanisms, and turning the connection into a proposal.
segments.zh: 这一设计为更广泛的自动化研究讨论增添了一个独特的问题。A-I Scientist强调从想法到实验再到写作的连贯流程，而IdeaScientist则把提案生成单独隔离出来，使其各阶段能在执行之前被逐一审视。它基于类比的方法也与创造性认知理论相呼应：有用的新颖性可以来自识别不同领域之间的共同结构。其实践贡献在于提供了一套可检验的工作流程，用于发现空白、寻找机制，并将这种关联转化为提案。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: There are important limits. The held-out set contains 277 methodological machine-learning papers from a retrospective period, so broader fields and kinds of scientific work remain untested. Training references are reconstructed from papers using language models, and the authors cannot rule out contamination in models’ stored knowledge. Scores also rely partly on language-model judges, whose agreement with people is imperfect. Future work should test whether these proposals withstand expert review and lead to reliable results when researchers implement them.
segments.zh: 当然也有一些重要的局限。留出集包含277篇来自回顾性时间段的方法学机器学习论文，所以更广泛的领域和不同类型的科研工作还没有得到检验。训练参考是用语言模型从论文中重建出来的，作者也无法排除模型存储知识中存在污染的可能。评分也部分依赖语言模型评审，而它们与人类判断的一致性并不完美。未来的工作应该检验这些提案能否经得起专家评审，以及当研究人员真正去实现它们时，能否带来可靠的结果。

segments.speaker: John
segments.en: The main takeaway is that scientific ideation can be studied as a sequence of inspectable decisions, not only as the opening stage of an automated experiment pipeline. IdeaScientist offers one way to connect evidence from nearby work with mechanisms from farther afield, while making the proposed transfer explicit enough to challenge. Its benchmark measures alignment with later research, not discovery itself, so the next step is testing whether these proposals help scientists do better work. Thanks for listening. If you have any further questions, ask our AI assistant or drop a comment.
segments.zh: 核心结论是，科学创意可以当作一连串可审视的决策来研究，而不只是自动化实验流程的开头阶段。IdeaScientist 提供了一种方式，把邻近工作的证据和更远领域的机制连接起来，同时让所提议的迁移足够明确，经得起质疑。它的基准衡量的是与后续研究的一致性，而不是发现本身，所以下一步要测试的是，这些提议能否帮助科学家做出更好的工作。感谢收听。如果还有问题，可以问我们的 AI 助手，或者留言评论。
